replication.published: train acc ~100% by ~1.4k epochs; test generalizes at ~10k (Fig. 2, wd=1, 30% split)
replication.criterion: test-95% epoch ≥ 3× train-99% epoch and final test acc > 99%, for every seed

replication.claim: The embedding is sparse in the Fourier basis
replication.criterion: ≤ 10 frequencies carry 90% of the norm in every seed

replication.claim: A handful of key frequencies; most neurons are single-frequency
replication.published: 5 key freqs {14, 35, 41, 42, 52} in their seed; 84.6% of neurons > 85% FVE from one frequency
replication.ours: key freqs per seed: 1, 21, 49 | 16, 17, 30, 55 | 6, 43, 48, 56; 75.0% of neurons periodic (seed 0)
replication.criterion: 3–7 key frequencies per seed and > 60% periodic neurons (exact frequencies are seed-dependent)

replication.claim: The key frequencies are causally necessary
replication.published: ablating key frequencies destroys performance; other frequencies don't matter (§5.2, Fig. 6)

replication.claim: Weight decay is needed for grokking
replication.published: no grokking without regularization in this setup (§5.3 / App.)
replication.ours: wd=0: final train 1.000, test 0.033 after 40000 epochs
